title: Economic activities and countries' development
competency: Relate economic activities to levels of development and compare agriculture in developed and developing countries.

keywords.def: Taking resources directly from the environment: agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining.
Adding value to products by processing them: manufacturing, construction, power production.
Support services that do not produce goods: transport, communication, trade, tourism, health, education.

en.text: Developed countries have large manufacturing industries; most people work in secondary activities and few in agriculture, yet modern methods give surplus food. In developing countries most people still work in agriculture, but production is low; agriculture can be over a quarter of national output.

screens.title: Few farmers, lots of food
screens.ask: In some rich countries, 2 in every 100 workers are farmers, yet they export food. How?
screens.after: Modern methods let few workers produce a lot. That is a mark of developed countries.
